correctness.rationale: For the displayed Kraus map, applying it to a diagonal telescopes the holding terms, giving the explicit Markov bidiagonal with forward coefficient a_n=δ_n/d. Strict moment log-convexity follows from Cauchy–Schwarz for a nonconstant squared radius; the ratios have limit 1 because the nth roots of the moments tend to 1 by support near radius one. The operator differs from bI+aB by a norm limit of finite-rank truncations. For the backward shift the open disk has index +1 by explicit bounded recurrence, and the rim has nonclosed range by finite-support tapering approximate eigenvectors at positive distance from its kernel. The eigenvector multiplier has limiting modulus |λ−b|/a; on the rim use |λ−β_n|≤a_n. Outside, a bounded eigenvector must terminate at λ=β_j, which lies outside exactly when δ_j>2. Cutting beyond j gives an invertible tail; the head has distinct diagonal entries, so the isolated eigenvalue is algebraically simple. The same cut and a Neumann series give the resolvent off the displayed spectrum. For beta weights the moments give δ_n=(n+A)/(n+1). The right mode decreases to its last nonzero index j; the left recurrence yields the stated alternating Pochhammer tail with absolute sum 2(1−r_j)^(−A−j−1) by differentiation of the binomial series. Their overlap is exactly one; aligning input signs attains the rank-one norm. At α=j+ε, 1−r_j=ε/(j+1+ε), and ε^(−ε)→1 supplies the sharp constant and exponent 2j+3.
